0.long_answer: The symptoms described—dizziness, dysarthria, hemiparesis, and paresthesia—are indicative of a stroke, particularly an ischemic stroke. Varicella-zoster virus can lead to a severe complication in the form of a cerebrovascular event. When VZV reactivates, it may cause inflammation of the cerebral blood vessels (vasculopathy), which can result in an ischemic stroke. This process disrupts normal blood flow to parts of the brain and produces the neurologic deficits mentioned.
